question: One question about your answer. You returned no_ladder. Which instruction in the request, and which words of the topic or the item, led you to decline? Quote them. If you cannot identify them, say so. Answer in at most 120 words.
reply:
I relied on the no-ladder rule: “the figure covers a period that is not one fiscal or calendar year … and neither the topic nor the item gives the day it is published.”

I applied it to the outcome’s words, “shipment volume from Q4 2026 through calendar 2027,” and the item’s statement, “The item gives no confirmation date.” On review, that was a mistake: the topic says its stated forecast periods “fix the check dates,” and the item gives a separate calendar-2027 forecast. Those words do not justify declining to set a ladder on that basis.

reply: I relied on the no-ladder rule: “the topic has no main figure or event, naming none, or naming several with none of them the main one.” I treated “commodity DRAM/graphics memory contract prices” as multiple figures with no main one. That was a misapplication: the topic’s settled-by material specifies “quarterly DRAM contract price releases,” which identifies commodity DRAM contract prices as the tracked figure; graphics memory and the shortage are related but separate parts.
